title: The breach dive tamed: the hold was paying 45 ms a frame for dust the fade discarded, and the opening frame was paying for shader links, first-use log reads and stone map uploads that now happen at boot
context: 2026-09-16-sixty-fps-under-the-horde left the breach dive shot (src/fx/dive-shot.js: the whole planet through the pre-roll, a 1.4 s dive to the sinkhole, a hold while the fodder emerge, a blend home) as the largest remaining hitch: 25 ms a frame at dpr 1 and 93 ms at dpr 2, and the QA playthrough had the sinkhole opening itself spike ~83 ms. The owner chose the shot ('the fast dive to the sinkhole as it opens felt like an event'); the task was to make it smooth without changing its composition or timing: no frame over 33 ms at dpr 2 through the dive, the opening spike under 50 ms.
outcome: MEASURED FIRST (artifacts/qa/dive-probe.mjs through the browser lock: every rAF frame through the shot with the gl draw counts of that frame per shader program, long tasks, fetches, the landmark tiers before and after, a CDP CPU profile split into the shot's windows, a schedule of draw-skipping experiments in the hold, and a full-size frame diff with and without a program). Two shots on the story route past the handover: sector 1's own first breach, and a real back-lane breach (backBreach) once the hull stands. BEFORE, dpr 2, back-lane shot: whole p50 19.4 / p95 79.9 / max 173.8; pre-roll p50 17.5 max 34; dive p50 18.5 max 46; HOLD p50 57.3 / p95 82.3 / max 174 (165 of 209 frames over 33 ms); the game's timer query read 22 -> 150 ms of GPU as the hold went on. Sector 1's own opening frame: 100.7 ms at dpr 1, 148 ms at dpr 2, with five program links (getProgramInfoLog 49 ms), the four stone maps' texSubImage2D (39 ms), bfsDist twice (13 ms) and the clearing scan (11 ms); then 56 ms + 32 ms frames as the dive passed the base and the landmarks' near tiers, mounted during the pre-roll, linked on their first draw. The near view drew ~100 calls and 1.3M triangles (the whole 71k-cell board's floor, walls and 715k line segments twice), not 5M: the 2026-09-16 figure was renderer.info summed across both composer passes plus the far view. WHAT THE HOLD WAS: skipping the smoke particle draws alone took the hold from 62-80 ms to 17 ms; skipping the post chain's full-screen passes did the same only because the GPU was saturated (the game's timer query read 100-150 ms while frames took 60-80). The particle fragment shader samples frame.uSceneDepth for its soft fade; nothing in the game binds a depth prepass, so three binds its all-zero empty texture, which unpacks to depth 0 (the near plane), softFade returns 0 and every fragment is discarded - after the smoke's fbm3 has been paid at 2880x1974 for ~100 puffs of 1.65 cells each, in both scene passes. A full-size frame diff with and without the particle draws sat on the motion floor (mean 0.13-0.15 of 255 vs 0.16-0.17 between two ordinary consecutive frames; max identical): nothing of them reached the screen. THE CHANGES: (1) src/sinkhole.js hides the particle meshes while frame.uSceneDepth is null (a host that binds a prepass gets them back untouched; the pinned src/fx/sinkhole tree is unchanged). (2) src/fx/shader-warm.js: a warmer that compiles a root's materials for the screen and for a linear target (r160 keys programs on the target's colour space; the bloom chain's scene passes render offscreen), polls COMPLETION_STATUS the way compileAsync does, then pulls every program's uniforms and attributes: three's first bind of a program reads the link log and both shader logs, four synchronous GPU-process round trips, and with every link done at boot the opening frame still stalled 49 ms on those. (3) src/game-breaches.js builds one hidden template sinkhole at boot, dressed as a real one (game look, one visible update so the sphere wraps are installed, one decal of each type acquired for the pass), hands it to the warmer and uploads the four stone maps one per frame once loaded; it is kept for the run because three frees a program with its last material. The wall debris's two-sided material goes through the same warmer. (4) src/fx/story-base.js: a landmark's near tier goes to the warmer as it mounts, hidden, and becomes the tier to swap to only once its programs are linked and first-used - the far tier stands a few frames longer, the swap is unchanged (a NOTE, not a silent change: strictly the far tier can be on screen a few frames more during a fly-by). (5) src/td-tab.js: the breach's clearing scan compares a dot against the unit normals instead of an acos of a freshly normalised centre per cell (11 -> ~1 ms). AFTER, dpr 2, back-lane shot: whole p50 17.3 / p95 23.5 / max 31.7 in the dive, hold p50 17.6 / p95 24.2, no frame over 33.4 ms in the shot; dpr 1: whole p50 16.7 / p95 18.6 / max 27.5, hold max 19.3. Sector 1's own opening frame: dpr 1 100.7 -> 42 ms (then, with first-use warming and the dot scan) dpr 2 148 -> 42 ms, no long task in the shot; the dive's pass over the base links nothing. td-tab unchanged at 13,505 lines. Not changed: the shot's poses, timing, the sinkhole's opening, the bloom chain.
alternatives: Rendering the dust at half resolution, fewer octaves, fewer puffs, or dropping it from the bloom pass: not done; the diff showed the dust never reached the screen, so hiding it while no depth is bound is pixel-identical, and a real soft-particle path (a depth prepass into frame.uSceneDepth) is the owner's call, with the fill cost in hand: ~45 ms a frame at dpr 2 for the settling dust from 5 cells up.
Freezing the landmark tiers through a shot: not needed once the near tier's programs are warmed before it can be swapped in; the swap distance and hysteresis are untouched.
Warming the sinkhole's programs at breach creation instead of boot: rejected; create() and the shot's first frame are the same frame, so the stall would only move onto the cut.

Staging rebuildAfterBreach and recomputePortalDist across frames: not done; the two BFS passes are ~9 ms of the opening frame on the 71k-cell planet and the frame is now under the 50 ms target without them.
compileAsync alone: tried first; the links moved off the opening frame but the frame still stalled 49 ms in getProgramInfoLog on first use, hence the warmer pulling uniforms and attributes itself.
evidence: artifacts/qa/dive-probe.mjs [label] [--dpr=2] [--profile-sector] [--no-skips] [--diff-only] through scripts/browser-lock.sh; outputs under artifacts/qa/dive-<label>-dpr<n>/ (per-shot json with every frame, cpuprofile, screenshots); artifacts/qa/prof-window.mjs and slow-frames.mjs read them back.
